claims.text: Transition-metal catalytic activity is governed by the metal electronic structure.
The d-band center position relative to the Fermi level governs catalytic activity by influencing adsorption strength.
Platinum, palladium, and nickel catalysts can have varying d-band center positions.
Alloying or strain engineering can systematically vary the d-band center position.
The d-band center controls overlap between metal electronic states and reactant molecular orbitals.
Changes in electronic-state and molecular-orbital overlap alter adsorption energies.
Changes in adsorption energies alter reaction kinetics.
Catalysts with d-band centers closer to the Fermi level will exhibit higher catalytic activity.
The predicted higher activity arises from optimal adsorption energies.
D-band centers too far from the Fermi level will reduce activity because adsorption is either too weak or too strong.
The hypothesis applies to reactions for which adsorption strength is a critical mechanistic factor.
The hypothesis applies to transition metals with partially filled d-orbitals.
The hypothesis may not apply when activity is dominated by mass transport limitations.
The hypothesis may not apply when activity is dominated by non-electronic structural effects.
A catalyst series should be tested under identical conditions while measuring d-band position, adsorption energies, and reaction rate or turnover frequency.
